claim: IL-10-producing CD4+ T cells in the salivary glands during chronic MCMV infection peak on day 14 post-infection.
source: Unlike mucosal sites in the respiratory tract (Zhang et al., 2019), ongoing viral replication in this model occurs primarily in the SGs, facilitated by the induction of CD4+ T cells that produce IL-10 (Humphreys et al., 2007), which peak on day 14 post-infection (p.i.) (Clement et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Clement et al., 2016, which provides published evidence for the timing of IL-10-producing CD4+ T cell peak.

claim: Approximately 10-30% of CD4+ T cells in the salivary glands are Thy1.1+ at day 14 post-infection with MCMV.
source: At this time point, we found that approximately 10–30% of CD4+ T cells in the SGs were Thy1.1+, of which ~95% displayed an effector memory phenotype (CD44hi CD62Llo) (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by data presented in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A, which shows flow cytometry measurements.

claim: Approximately 95% of Thy1.1+ CD4+ T cells display an effector memory phenotype (CD44hi CD62Llo).
source: At this time point, we found that approximately 10–30% of CD4+ T cells in the SGs were Thy1.1+, of which ~95% displayed an effector memory phenotype (CD44hi CD62Llo) (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by data presented in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A showing phenotypic characterization.

claim: IL-10-producing CD4+ T cells universally express Thy1.1 after polyclonal stimulation.
source: IL-10-producing CD4+ T cells were also induced by polyclonal stimulation and universally expressed Thy1.1 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B demonstrating IL-10 and Thy1.1 coexpression.

claim: Thy1.1+ CD4+ T cells are transcriptionally distinct from Thy1.1− CD4+ T cells.
source: Principal component analysis (PCA) of the RNA-seq data revealed that Thy1.1+ CD4+ T cells were transcriptionally distinct from Thy1.1− CD4+ T cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by RNA-seq data analyzed via PCA and shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Il10 is highly upregulated in Thy1.1+ CD4+ T cells compared to Thy1.1− CD4+ T cells.
source: As expected, Il10 was highly upregulated in Thy1.1+ CD4+ T cells (Figure 1A), and chromatin was more open in the Il10 promoter region compared with Thy1.1− CD4+ T cells (Figure 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 1A and ATAC-seq data in Figure 1B.

claim: Chromatin is more open in the Il10 promoter region in Thy1.1+ CD4+ T cells compared with Thy1.1− CD4+ T cells.
source: As expected, Il10 was highly upregulated in Thy1.1+ CD4+ T cells (Figure 1A), and chromatin was more open in the Il10 promoter region compared with Thy1.1− CD4+ T cells (Figure 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by ATAC-seq data shown in Figure 1B demonstrating chromatin accessibility.

claim: Genes associated with localization and cell migration are upregulated in Thy1.1+ CD4+ T cells.
source: Genes associated with localization and cell migration (Ccl7, Cxcl2, Cxcl12, Ccl5, Cxcl14, Ccl28, Ccl12, Ccr1, and Ccr5), cell signaling (Ceacam1, Havcr2, Tigit, Lag3, Cd40, Cd36, and Itgb4), regulation of cellular processes (Prdm1, Gata2, Yes1, Card10, and Il33), and metabolism (Elovl7, Galnt3, Car13, Aldh1l1, and Ildrl), including glycolysis and the tricarboxylic acid cycle (Fbp2 and Sdhc), oxidative phosphorylation (Osgin1), and the mitochondrial respiratory chain (Mt-Nd1, Ndufs6, Ndufb8, Uqcrfs1, and Uqcr11), were also upregulated in Thy1.1+ CD4+ T cells, alongside genes associated with activation (Fgl2, Cxcr2, and Nfil3) and antiviral effector functions (Gzmb, Prf1, Gzmk, and Lyz2) (Figure 1A, C, D and Figure 1—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: The claim is supported by RNA-seq data shown in multiple figures (1A, C, D and supplement 1D).

claim: Genes associated with antiviral effector functions (Gzmb, Prf1, Gzmk, and Lyz2) are upregulated in Thy1.1+ CD4+ T cells.
source: Genes associated with localization and cell migration (Ccl7, Cxcl2, Cxcl12, Ccl5, Cxcl14, Ccl28, Ccl12, Ccr1, and Ccr5), cell signaling (Ceacam1, Havcr2, Tigit, Lag3, Cd40, Cd36, and Itgb4), regulation of cellular processes (Prdm1, Gata2, Yes1, Card10, and Il33), and metabolism (Elovl7, Galnt3, Car13, Aldh1l1, and Ildrl), including glycolysis and the tricarboxylic acid cycle (Fbp2 and Sdhc), oxidative phosphorylation (Osgin1), and the mitochondrial respiratory chain (Mt-Nd1, Ndufs6, Ndufb8, Uqcrfs1, and Uqcr11), were also upregulated in Thy1.1+ CD4+ T cells, alongside genes associated with activation (Fgl2, Cxcr2, and Nfil3) and antiviral effector functions (Gzmb, Prf1, Gzmk, and Lyz2) (Figure 1A, C, D and Figure 1—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: The claim is supported by RNA-seq data showing upregulation of effector genes.

claim: Thy1.1+ CD4+ T cells lack gene signatures classically associated with cytotoxic CD4+ T cells, such as upregulation of Klrc1 and Crtam.
source: These latter gene profiles suggested the potential for cytolytic activity, but we found no evidence of a concomitant increase in the expression levels of granzyme B protein among Thy1.1+ CD4+ T cells (data not shown), which also lacked gene signatures classically associated with cytotoxic CD4+ T cells, such as the upregulation of Klrc1 and Crtam (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.7243956).
evidence: The claim is supported by RNA-seq data deposited at the provided DOI.

claim: Il7 and Tcf1/7 are downregulated in Thy1.1+ CD4+ T cells at both the transcript and protein levels.
source: Other genes that were downregulated in Thy1.1+ CD4+ T cells included Il7 and Tcf1/7 (Figure 1A, D), which extended to the protein level (Figure 1F).
evidence: The claim is supported by RNA-seq data (Figure 1A, D) and flow cytometry data (Figure 1F).

claim: The downregulation of IL-7R and TCF1/7 in Thy1.1+ CD4+ T cells coincides temporally with the rapid contraction of virus-specific IL-10-producing CD4+ T cells during early stages of viral chronicity.
source: The relative underexpression of these cell survival-associated factors coincided temporally with the rapid contraction of virus-specific IL-10-producing CD4+ T cells that typically occurs during the early stages of viral chronicity (Clement et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by inference from the data and citation to Clement et al., 2016.

claim: Thy1.1+ and Thy1.1− CD4+ T cells express similar levels of transcripts encoding DR5.
source: In contrast, Thy1.1+ and Thy1.1− CD4+ T cells expressed similar levels of transcripts encoding DR5 (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.7243956), which engages natural killer (NK) cell-expressed TRAIL and induces CD4+ T cell death in the SGs (Schuster et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by RNA-seq data deposited at the provided DOI and citation to Schuster et al., 2014.

claim: MCMV-induced Thy1.1+ CD4+ T cells downregulate the exhaustion-associated transcription factor Tox1.
source: Counterintuitively, we found that MCMV-induced Thy1.1+ CD4+ T cells downregulated the exhaustion-associated transcription factor Tox1 but nonetheless expressed a module of inhibitory genes, including Lag3, Fgl2, Havcr2, and Entpd1 (Figure 1D).
evidence: The claim is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: MCMV-induced Thy1.1+ CD4+ T cells express a module of inhibitory genes, including Lag3, Fgl2, Havcr2, and Entpd1.
source: Counterintuitively, we found that MCMV-induced Thy1.1+ CD4+ T cells downregulated the exhaustion-associated transcription factor Tox1 but nonetheless expressed a module of inhibitory genes, including Lag3, Fgl2, Havcr2, and Entpd1 (Figure 1D).
evidence: The claim is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Inhibitory molecules LAG-3, PD-1, TIM-3, CD39, and TIGIT are expressed at the protein level in Thy1.1+ CD4+ T cells.
source: These inhibitory molecules were also expressed at the protein level, alongside PD-1 (Figure 1G and Figure 1—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 1G and Figure 1—figure supplement 1F.

claim: Thy1.1+ CD4+ T cells express LAG-3 and PD-1 more commonly than Thy1.1− CD4+ T cells after preselection based on IFNγ induction.
source: In addition, differential bystander activation seemed unlikely, because Thy1.1+ CD4+ T cells expressed LAG-3 and PD-1 more commonly than Thy1.1− CD4+ T cells after preselection based on the induction of IFNγ (Figure 1—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1E.

claim: IL-10-producing CD4+ T cells exhibit a highly differentiated TH1-like profile during chronic infection with MCMV.
source: Collectively, these data showed that IL-10-producing CD4+ T cells exhibited a highly differentiated TH1-like profile, characterized by the upregulation of various inhibitory molecules and the downmodulation of IFNγ expression lacking concordance with known signatures of exhaustion, during chronic infection with MCMV.
evidence: The claim is a summary inference from multiple data types presented in the manuscript.

claim: IL-10-producing CD4+ T cells recognize a broad range of viral antigens during chronic infection with MCMV.
source: IL-10-producing CD4+ T cells recognize a broad range of viral antigens during chronic infection with MCMV (Clement et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Clement et al., 2016.

claim: The repertoires of Thy1.1+ CD4+ T cells are less diverse than the repertoires of Thy1.1− CD4+ T cells.
source: The repertoires of Thy1.1+ CD4+ T cells were less diverse and incorporated more prominent clonal expansions compared with the repertoires of Thy1.1− CD4+ T cells (Figure 2A, B and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by TCR-seq data shown in Figure 2A, B and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Thy1.1+ CD4+ T cells incorporate more prominent clonal expansions compared with Thy1.1− CD4+ T cells.
source: The repertoires of Thy1.1+ CD4+ T cells were less diverse and incorporated more prominent clonal expansions compared with the repertoires of Thy1.1− CD4+ T cells (Figure 2A, B and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by TCR-seq data showing clonality metrics.

claim: The number of nucleotide variants encoding each CDR3α and CDR3β amino acid sequence is higher overall among Thy1.1+ CD4+ T cells versus Thy1.1− CD4+ T cells.
source: First, the number of nucleotide variants that encoded each complementarity-determining region (CDR)3α and CDR3β amino acid sequence, an indicator of antigen-specific convergence (Logunova et al., 2020), was higher overall among Thy1.1+ CD4+ T cells versus Thy1.1− CD4+ T cells (Figure 2C).
evidence: The claim is supported by TCR-seq data shown in Figure 2C and citation to Logunova et al., 2020.

claim: There are differences in Trbv gene use that distinguish Thy1.1+ CD4+ T cells from Thy1.1− CD4+ T cells, with a general preference for Trbv3, Trbv5, and Trbv31.
source: Second, there were some differences in Trbv gene use that distinguished Thy1.1+ CD4+ T cells from Thy1.1− CD4+ T cells, albeit with a general preference for Trbv3, Trbv5, and Trbv31 (Figure 2D).
evidence: The claim is supported by TCR-seq data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Clusters of homologous TCRβ variants are detected predominantly among Thy1.1+ CD4+ T cells.
source: Third, clusters of homologous TCRβ variants, identified using the statistical model ALICE (Pogorelyy et al., 2019), were detected predominantly among Thy1.1+ CD4+ T cells (Figure 2E–G).
evidence: The claim is supported by TCR-seq data analyzed using ALICE and shown in Figure 2E–G, with citation to Pogorelyy et al., 2019.

claim: The TCRα and TCRβ repertoires overlap considerably between Thy1.1+ CD4+ T cells and Thy1.1− CD4+ T cells.
source: It should be noted that none of these differences were absolute. For example, the clusters of TCRβ variants identified among Thy1.1+ CD4+ T cells also occurred at lower cumulative frequencies among Thy1.1− CD4+ T cells (Figure 2E–G), and the TCRα and TCRβ repertoires overlapped considerably between Thy1.1+ CD4+ T cells and Thy1.1− CD4+ T cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by TCR-seq data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claim: There are no prominent differences in the physicochemical properties of amino acids in the central parts of the CDR3α and CDR3β loops between Thy1.1+ CD4+ T cells and Thy1.1− CD4+ T cells.
source: Moreover, there were no prominent differences in the physicochemical properties of amino acids in the central parts of the CDR3α and CDR3β loops, which generally differ among functionally discrete subsets of CD4+ T cells (Kasatskaya et al., 2020), to indicate an ontogenetic divergence between Thy1.1+ CD4+ T cells and Thy1.1− CD4+ T cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by TCR-seq data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1C and citation to Kasatskaya et al., 2020.

claim: Common molecular signatures predominate among Thy1.1+ CD4+ T cells, consistent with an antigen-driven process of differentiation leading to IL-10 production.
source: Collectively, these data revealed the presence of common molecular signatures that predominated among Thy1.1+ CD4+ T cells, consistent with the notion of an antigen-driven process of differentiation leading to the production of IL-10.
evidence: The claim is an inference from the TCR-seq data presented.

claim: Thy1.1+ CD4+ T cells significantly upregulate Arg1.
source: Our analysis of inhibitory gene expression revealed one particularly intriguing feature, namely that Thy1.1+ CD4+ T cells significantly upregulated Arg1 (Figure 1D).
evidence: The claim is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Arg1 promotes the catalytic breakdown of L-arginine.
source: Arg1 promotes the catalytic breakdown of L-arginine (Munder, 2009) and has been shown to inhibit the proliferation of T cells (Czystowska-Kuzmicz et al., 2019; Rodriguez et al., 2004; Rodriguez et al., 2002).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Munder, 2009 and other studies.

claim: Arg1 has been shown to inhibit the proliferation of T cells.
source: Arg1 promotes the catalytic breakdown of L-arginine (Munder, 2009) and has been shown to inhibit the proliferation of T cells (Czystowska-Kuzmicz et al., 2019; Rodriguez et al., 2004; Rodriguez et al., 2002).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to multiple studies.

claim: Arg1 is expressed at the protein level by CD4+ T cells in the salivary glands during chronic MCMV infection.
source: To address this knowledge gap, we first confirmed expression at the protein level via Western blotting (Figure 3A) in experiments incorporating control mice lacking the ability to express Arg1 in the CD4+ lineage (Cd4Cre/+Arg1flox/flox).
evidence: The claim is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Chromatin is open around Arg1 in Thy1.1+ CD4+ T cells.
source: We then revealed the open chromatin structure around Arg1 in Thy1.1+ CD4+ T cells (Figure 3B) and further probed the expression of Arg1 versus Thy1.1 among CD4+ T cells via flow cytometry (Figure 3C).
evidence: The claim is supported by ATAC-seq data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Arg1 is expressed by CD4+ T cells almost exclusively in the salivary glands.
source: Our data showed that Arg1 was expressed by CD4+ T cells almost exclusively in the SGs (Figure 3A, C).
evidence: The claim is supported by Western blot and flow cytometry data shown in Figure 3A and 3C.

claim: Only CD4+ T cells contribute significantly to Arg1 protein concentrations in SG homogenates during chronic infection with MCMV.
source: Depletion experiments nonetheless revealed that only CD4+ T cells contributed significantly to Arg1 protein concentrations in SG homogenates during chronic infection with MCMV (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by depletion experiments shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1B.

claim: High-dose OVA323–339 in combination with IL-12 induces the development of CD4+ T cells that express Arg1 and IL-10 in vitro.
source: Despite constitutively high expression levels of Arg1, only high-dose OVA323–339 in combination with IL-12 induced the development of CD4+ T cells that expressed Arg1 and IL-10, and importantly, all IL-10-producing CD4+ T cells coexpressed Arg1 (Figure 3D).
evidence: The claim is supported by in vitro culture data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: All IL-10-producing CD4+ T cells coexpress Arg1 in vitro.
source: Despite constitutively high expression levels of Arg1, only high-dose OVA323–339 in combination with IL-12 induced the development of CD4+ T cells that expressed Arg1 and IL-10, and importantly, all IL-10-producing CD4+ T cells coexpressed Arg1 (Figure 3D).
evidence: The claim is supported by in vitro culture data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Arg1 protein concentrations in culture supernatants increase substantially after stimulation with high-dose OVA323–339 in the presence of IL-12.
source: Arg1 protein concentrations in culture supernatants also increased substantially after stimulation with high-dose OVA323–339 in the presence of IL-12 (Figure 3E).
evidence: The claim is supported by ELISA data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: Arg1 expression is a hallmark of IL-10-producing CD4+ T cells, which develop almost exclusively in the salivary glands during chronic infection with MCMV.
source: Collectively, these data suggested that Arg1 expression was a hallmark of IL-10-producing CD4+ T cells, which developed almost exclusively in the SGs during chronic infection with MCMV.
evidence: The claim is an inference from the data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Lineage-specific deletion of Arg1 does not impact the function or phenotype of CD4+ T cells in naive mice.
source: Lineage-specific deletion of Arg1 did not impact the function or phenotype of CD4+ T cells in naive mice (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C, D).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1C, D.

claim: Higher numbers of IFNγ-expressing CD4+ T cells are observed in the salivary glands of Cd4Cre/+Arg1flox/flox versus Cd4+/+Arg1flox/flox mice during chronic MCMV infection.
source: Higher numbers of IFNγ-expressing CD4+ T cells (Figure 4A) and higher frequencies of proliferating (Ki-67+) CD4+ T cells (Figure 4B) were nonetheless observed after viral antigen stimulation in the SGs of Cd4Cre/+Arg1flox/flox versus Cd4+/+Arg1flox/flox mice during the chronic phase of infection with MCMV.
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Higher frequencies of proliferating (Ki-67+) CD4+ T cells are observed in the salivary glands of Cd4Cre/+Arg1flox/flox versus Cd4+/+Arg1flox/flox mice during chronic MCMV infection.
source: Higher numbers of IFNγ-expressing CD4+ T cells (Figure 4A) and higher frequencies of proliferating (Ki-67+) CD4+ T cells (Figure 4B) were nonetheless observed after viral antigen stimulation in the SGs of Cd4Cre/+Arg1flox/flox versus Cd4+/+Arg1flox/flox mice during the chronic phase of infection with MCMV.
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Arg1 inhibits the proliferation of CD4+ T cells in vivo.
source: These data suggested that Arg1 inhibited the proliferation of CD4+ T cells in vivo, consistent with a previous in vitro study (Munder et al., 2006).
evidence: The claim is an inference from the data and supported by citation to Munder et al., 2006.

claim: Higher numbers of virus-specific CD8+ T cells are detected in the spleens of Cd4Cre/+Arg1flox/flox versus Cd4+/+Arg1flox/flox mice on day 30 post-infection.
source: Similarly, higher numbers of virus-specific CD8+ T cells, quantified using tetrameric antigen probes, were detected in the spleens of Cd4Cre/+Arg1flox/flox versus Cd4+/+Arg1flox/flox mice on day 30 p.i. (Figure 4C).
evidence: The claim is supported by tetramer staining data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Arg1 deletion has no significant impact on the development of virus-specific IL-10-producing CD4+ T cells in the salivary glands.
source: In contrast, Arg1 deletion had no significant impact on the development of virus-specific IL-10-producing CD4+ T cells in the SGs (Figure 4D).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: Viral shedding in the saliva is reduced in Cd4Cre/+Arg1flox/flox versus Cd4+/+Arg1flox/flox mice during the chronic phase of infection with MCMV.
source: Accordingly, we found that viral shedding in the saliva (Figure 4E) and viral replication in the SGs (Figure 4F) were reduced in Cd4Cre/+Arg1flox/flox versus Cd4+/+Arg1flox/flox mice during the chronic phase of infection with MCMV.
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 4E.

claim: Viral replication in the salivary glands is reduced in Cd4Cre/+Arg1flox/flox versus Cd4+/+Arg1flox/flox mice during the chronic phase of infection with MCMV.
source: Accordingly, we found that viral shedding in the saliva (Figure 4E) and viral replication in the SGs (Figure 4F) were reduced in Cd4Cre/+Arg1flox/flox versus Cd4+/+Arg1flox/flox mice during the chronic phase of infection with MCMV.
evidence: The claim is supported by plaque assay data shown in Figure 4F.

claim: No differences in viral replication are observed between Cd4Cre/+Arg1flox/flox and control mice at day 14 post-infection.
source: Importantly, no differences in viral replication were observed between Cd4Cre/+Arg1flox/flox and control mice at an earlier time point (day 14 p.i.) (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A), and deletion of Arg1 in myeloid cells, achieved using Lyz2Cre/+Arg1flox/flox mice, had no impact on viral shedding in the saliva or viral replication in the SGs (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B, C).
evidence: The claim is supported by plaque assay data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Deletion of Arg1 in myeloid cells has no impact on viral shedding in the saliva or viral replication in the salivary glands.
source: Importantly, no differences in viral replication were observed between Cd4Cre/+Arg1flox/flox and control mice at an earlier time point (day 14 p.i.) (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A), and deletion of Arg1 in myeloid cells, achieved using Lyz2Cre/+Arg1flox/flox mice, had no impact on viral shedding in the saliva or viral replication in the SGs (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B, C).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1B, C.

claim: There is no evidence that Cd4Cre/+Arg1flox/flox mice are more susceptible to virus-induced autoimmunity.
source: Of note, there was also no evidence that Cd4Cre/+Arg1flox/flox mice were more susceptible to virus-induced autoimmunity, as indicated by anti-Sjögrens syndrome antigen (SSA) titers comparable to those observed in Cd4+/+Arg1flox/flox mice (Figure 4—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: The claim is supported by ELISA data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1D.

claim: Arg1 expression by CD4+ T cells selectively inhibits the accumulation of virus-specific CD4+ and CD8+ T cells in the salivary glands, leading to suboptimal immune control of viral replication during chronic infection with MCMV.
source: Collectively, these data indicated that Arg1 expression by CD4+ T cells selectively inhibited the accumulation of virus-specific CD4+ and CD8+ T cells in the SGs, leading to suboptimal immune control of viral replication during chronic infection with MCMV.
evidence: The claim is an inference from the data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Thy1.1+ CD4+ T cells express higher amounts of T-bet at the protein level than Thy1.1− CD4+ T cells.
source: In line with our previous work (Clement et al., 2016), we noted that Thy1.1+ CD4+ T cells expressed higher amounts of T-bet at the protein level than Thy1.1− CD4+ T cells (Figure 5A), and concordantly, we found that open chromatin was enriched in the Tbx21 region of Thy1.1+ CD4+ T cells versus Thy1.1− CD4+ T cells (Figure 5B).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 5A and citation to Clement et al., 2016.

claim: Open chromatin is enriched in the Tbx21 region of Thy1.1+ CD4+ T cells versus Thy1.1− CD4+ T cells.
source: In line with our previous work (Clement et al., 2016), we noted that Thy1.1+ CD4+ T cells expressed higher amounts of T-bet at the protein level than Thy1.1− CD4+ T cells (Figure 5A), and concordantly, we found that open chromatin was enriched in the Tbx21 region of Thy1.1+ CD4+ T cells versus Thy1.1− CD4+ T cells (Figure 5B).
evidence: The claim is supported by ATAC-seq data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: No differences in expression intensity are observed for Eomesodermin (Eomes) between Thy1.1+ and Thy1.1− CD4+ T cells.
source: No such differences in expression intensity were observed for the related T-box transcription factor Eomesodermin (Eomes) (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A, B), which promotes the development of Tr1 cells (Roessner et al., 2021; Zhang et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1A, B and citations.

claim: There is considerable overlap between the gene expression profiles of Thy1.1+ CD4+ T cells and T-bet-orchestrated CD4+ TH1 cells generated in vitro.
source: We also detected considerable overlap between the gene expression profiles of Thy1.1+ CD4+ T cells and T-bet-orchestrated CD4+ TH1 cells generated in vitro (Zhu et al., 2012; Figure 5C).
evidence: The claim is supported by comparison of RNA-seq data shown in Figure 5C and citation to Zhu et al., 2012.

claim: T-bet suppresses the expression of TCF1/7 and IL-7R.
source: Moreover, T-bet suppresses the expression of TCF1/7 and IL-7R (Dominguez et al., 2015; Oestreich et al., 2011), mimicking key phenotypic features of Thy1.1+ CD4+ T cells (Figure 1D, F).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Dominguez et al., 2015 and Oestreich et al., 2011.

claim: CD4-specific T-bet depletion reduces the accumulation of virus-specific IL-10-producing CD4+ T cells by day 14 post-infection.
source: CD4-specific T-bet depletion reduced the accumulation of virus-specific IL-10-producing CD4+ T cells (Figure 6A) and Arg1+ CD4+ T cells by day 14 p.i. (Figure 6B, C).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: CD4-specific T-bet depletion reduces the accumulation of Arg1+ CD4+ T cells by day 14 post-infection.
source: CD4-specific T-bet depletion reduced the accumulation of virus-specific IL-10-producing CD4+ T cells (Figure 6A) and Arg1+ CD4+ T cells by day 14 p.i. (Figure 6B, C).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 6B, C.

claim: T-bet does not directly stimulate the expression of IL-10 and Arg1.
source: However, it seemed unlikely that T-bet directly stimulated the expression of IL-10 and Arg1, because the corresponding binding motifs were not preferentially accessible in the Il10 and Arg1 regions (Figure 1B and Figure 3B).
evidence: The claim is an inference from ATAC-seq data shown in Figure 1B and Figure 3B.

claim: T-bet depletion is associated with a shift toward a less differentiated phenotype in CD4+ T cells.
source: Instead, we observed a shift toward a less differentiated phenotype in Cd4CreERT2/+Tbx21flox/flox mice (Figure 6D–G), with decreased expression of CD44 (Figure 6D) and PD-1 (Figure 6E) and increased expression of CD62L (Figure 6F) and IL-7R (Figure 6G) in the absence of T-bet.
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 6D–G.

claim: T-bet depletion is associated with increased numbers of virus-specific IFNγ-expressing CD4+ T cells.
source: In addition, T-bet depletion was associated with increased numbers of virus-specific IFNγ-expressing CD4+ T cells (Figure 6H) and enhanced control of viral replication in the SGs (Figure 6I), as well as reduced salivary shedding of MCMV (Figure 6J).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 6H.

claim: T-bet depletion is associated with enhanced control of viral replication in the salivary glands.
source: In addition, T-bet depletion was associated with increased numbers of virus-specific IFNγ-expressing CD4+ T cells (Figure 6H) and enhanced control of viral replication in the SGs (Figure 6I), as well as reduced salivary shedding of MCMV (Figure 6J).
evidence: The claim is supported by plaque assay data shown in Figure 6I.

claim: T-bet depletion is associated with reduced salivary shedding of MCMV.
source: In addition, T-bet depletion was associated with increased numbers of virus-specific IFNγ-expressing CD4+ T cells (Figure 6H) and enhanced control of viral replication in the SGs (Figure 6I), as well as reduced salivary shedding of MCMV (Figure 6J).
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 6J.

claim: CD4-specific T-bet depletion is no longer protective by day 28 post-infection.
source: In accordance with the observation that IL-10-producing CD4+ T cells occur transiently during the early stages of viral chronicity (Clement et al., 2016), we also found that CD4-specific T-bet depletion was no longer protective by day 28 p.i. (Figure 6J and Figure 5—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 6J and Figure 5—figure supplement 1D, and citation to Clement et al., 2016.

claim: T-bet exhibits dual functionality under conditions of recurrent antigen stimulation, concurrently driving the accumulation of virus-specific TH1 responses and promoting the development of Arg1+ IL-10-producing CD4+ T cells.
source: Collectively, these results suggested that T-bet exhibited dual functionality under conditions of recurrent antigen stimulation, concurrently driving the accumulation of virus-specific TH1 responses and promoting the development of Arg1+ IL-10-producing CD4+ T cells, which together shaped immune control of viral replication during the early stages of chronic infection with MCMV.
evidence: The claim is an inference from the data presented in the manuscript.

claim: IL-10-producing CD4+ T cells are highly differentiated TH1-like cells that occur transiently at mucosal sites of viral persistence under the strict governance of T-bet.
source: In this study, we identified IL-10-producing CD4+ T cells as highly differentiated TH1-like cells, which occurred transiently at mucosal sites of viral persistence under the strict governance of T-bet.
evidence: The claim is a summary of the study's findings.

claim: IL-10-producing CD4+ T cells express the metabolic enzyme Arg1.
source: These cells also expressed the metabolic enzyme Arg1.
evidence: The claim is supported by data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Arg1 expression is a critical immune regulatory function of CD4+ T cells, suppressing antiviral immunity and facilitating viral chronicity in the context of infection with MCMV.
source: Further investigation revealed that Arg1 expression was a critical immune regulatory function of CD4+ T cells, suppressing antiviral immunity and facilitating viral chronicity in the context of infection with MCMV.
evidence: The claim is a summary of the study's findings.

claim: Arg1 expression by human CD4+ T cells in vitro has been reported to be lacking.
source: Our finding that Arg1 was one of the putative immune regulatory genes expressed by IL-10-producing CD4+ T cells was initially counterintuitive, given the reported lack of Arg1 protein expression by human CD4+ T cells in vitro (Geiger et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Geiger et al., 2016.

claim: Arg1 expression by CD4+ and CD8+ T cells has been described in patients with sepsis.
source: However, Arg1 expression by CD4+ and CD8+ T cells has been described in patients with sepsis (Washburn et al., 2019), indicating a potential role for generic infectious stimuli and/or an antigen-driven process mediated via the TCR.
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Washburn et al., 2019.

claim: CD4+ T cells secrete Arg1 in soluble form in vivo.
source: Importantly, we demonstrated that Arg1 was expressed at the protein level, both in secreted form and intracellularly.
evidence: The claim is supported by data presented in the manuscript.

claim: CD4+ T cells secrete far greater amounts of soluble Arg1 than CD8+ T cells in the milieu of the salivary glands.
source: Our flow cytometry experiments also suggested that CD8+ T cells could express Arg1, albeit with the caveat of suboptimal visualization, but importantly, CD4+ T cells secreted far greater amounts of soluble Arg1, at least in the milieu of the SGs.
evidence: The claim is an inference from flow cytometry and depletion experiments.

claim: L-arginine deficiency results in cell cycle arrest via the downregulation of CD3ζ, a key component of the TCR.
source: L-arginine deficiency results in cell cycle arrest via the downregulation of CD3ζ, a key component of the TCR (Rodriguez et al., 2002), and T cell proliferation is impaired in the absence of L-arginine (Rodriguez et al., 2007).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Rodriguez et al., 2002 and 2007.

claim: T cell proliferation is impaired in the absence of L-arginine.
source: L-arginine deficiency results in cell cycle arrest via the downregulation of CD3ζ, a key component of the TCR (Rodriguez et al., 2002), and T cell proliferation is impaired in the absence of L-arginine (Rodriguez et al., 2007).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Rodriguez et al., 2007.

claim: Improved control of viral replication in mice lacking Arg1+ CD4+ T cells is associated with increased numbers of MCMV-specific effector CD4+ T cells.
source: In line with these observations, we found that improved control of viral replication in mice lacking Arg1+ CD4+ T cells was associated with increased numbers of MCMV-specific effector CD4+ T cells, which are known to limit viral replication in the SGs (Lucin et al., 1992; Walton et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is an inference from the data and supported by citations to Lucin et al., 1992 and Walton et al., 2011.

claim: The acquisition of Arg1 expression by highly differentiated CD4+ T cells impinges on antiviral immunity, representing an inhibitory mechanism that operates alongside the production of IL-10.

evidence: The claim is an inference from the data and supported by citations.

claim: Regulatory T cells may act similarly to Arg1+ CD4+ T cells via the expression of Arg2.

claim: IL-10 is regulated by a number of transcription factors, including those required for T cell differentiation, and is induced downstream of the TCR.

claim: T-bet promotes the development of IL-10-producing CD4+ T cells during chronic infection with MCMV.
source: Our discovery that T-bet promotes the development of IL-10-producing CD4+ T cells aligns with the concept that chronic antigen stimulation can trigger a negative feedback loop via these mechanisms, which concurrently drive activation and differentiation.
evidence: The claim is an inference from the data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Deletion of T-bet after acute infection limits the accumulation of highly differentiated CD4+ T cells, including those expressing Arg1 and IL-10.
source: However, we did find that deletion of T-bet after acute infection limited the accumulation of highly differentiated CD4+ T cells, including those expressing Arg1 and IL-10.
evidence: The claim is supported by data presented in the manuscript.

claim: T-bet promotes the differentiation of CD8+ T cells.
source: In line with this observation, which suggested a differentiation-linked process of functional remodeling driven by chronic antigen exposure, T-bet is known to promote the differentiation of CD8+ T cells (Dominguez et al., 2015; Omilusik et al., 2015) and inhibit the expression of TCF1/7 (Omilusik et al., 2015) and IL-7R (Intlekofer et al., 2007), both of which were downregulated among Arg1+ IL-10-producing CD4+ T cells induced by MCMV.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Dominguez et al., 2015 and Omilusik et al., 2015.

claim: T-bet inhibits the expression of TCF1/7.
source: In line with this observation, which suggested a differentiation-linked process of functional remodeling driven by chronic antigen exposure, T-bet is known to promote the differentiation of CD8+ T cells (Dominguez et al., 2015; Omilusik et al., 2015) and inhibit the expression of TCF1/7 (Omilusik et al., 2015) and IL-7R (Intlekofer et al., 2007), both of which were downregulated among Arg1+ IL-10-producing CD4+ T cells induced by MCMV.
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Omilusik et al., 2015.

claim: T-bet inhibits the expression of IL-7R.
source: In line with this observation, which suggested a differentiation-linked process of functional remodeling driven by chronic antigen exposure, T-bet is known to promote the differentiation of CD8+ T cells (Dominguez et al., 2015; Omilusik et al., 2015) and inhibit the expression of TCF1/7 (Omilusik et al., 2015) and IL-7R (Intlekofer et al., 2007), both of which were downregulated among Arg1+ IL-10-producing CD4+ T cells induced by MCMV.

claim: Mucosal IL-10-producing CD4+ T cells do not coexpress CD49b and LAG-3, unlike classical Tr1 cells.
source: In contrast to Tr1 cells (Gagliani et al., 2013), IL-10-producing CD4+ T cells in the SGs do not coexpress CD49b and LAG-3 (Clement et al., 2016), highlighting the diverse nature of regulatory CD4+ T cells defined by the secretion of IL-10 (Brockmann et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Gagliani et al., 2013, Clement et al., 2016, and Brockmann et al., 2018.

claim: IL-10-producing CD4+ T cells in the salivary glands express multiple inhibitory receptors, including LAG-3.
source: However, these cells do express multiple inhibitory receptors, including LAG-3, alongside other markers that typically characterize Tr1 cells, such as CCR5 and granzyme K (Brockmann et al., 2018; Roessner et al., 2021; Thelen et al., 2023).
evidence: The claim is supported by data in the manuscript and citations.

claim: Mucosal IL-10-producing CD4+ T cells may develop along similar lines to conventional Tr1 cells, which differentiate under the control of Eomes in conjunction with Blimp-1.
